offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The provider redelivered the webhook for evt_000281 (payment.succeeded, pay_000259, $157.18). The two deliveries arrived about 0.5 s apart. webhook-receiver accepted both and queued each one, so the event sits on provider-events at partition 1, offsets 120 and 121. ledger-consumer then booked it twice, as transactions 281 and 282. That puts our ledger $157.18 ahead of the provider and fails posted_exactly_once and matches_provider. payment-confirmer handled the same duplicate correctly and returned already_confirmed. So the bug is in the ledger's idempotency. On the second delivery it did no event_id check, and the unique constraint on transactions.event_id did not stop it either. The ledger does report already_processed for some events, so its dedup works for some duplicates. One explanation is that it dedups on Kafka offset or message, not on provider event_id. evidence.shows: Symptom confirmed after settling. evt_000281 is posted 2 times (transactions 281 and 282). The ledger is +$15,718 cents over the provider, all on pay_000259. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds agree with the provider.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000281 twice: at 20:08:00.097 to offset 120 and at 20:08:00.604 to offset 121, with different trace ids. This is a provider redelivery, and the receiver does not dedup it.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000281 at both offsets 120 and 121.

In the trace for offset 121, ledger-consumer goes straight to INSERT transactions and INSERT entries, with no visible event_id lookup, and its outcome is 'posted'. In the same trace, payment-confirmer's outcome is already_confirmed.
Over the last 10 minutes, the ledger reports some already_processed outcomes (17) and 485 posted, so its dedup catches some duplicates and missed this one.
ledger-consumer logged no warnings or errors in the last hour, so the double posting raised no error.
recent_deploys failed because Docker did not answer, so I could not check whether a ledger-consumer handler change caused this.

proposed_fix.summary: 1. Once Docker responds, check recent_deploys for a ledger-consumer LEDGER_HANDLER change. If one exists, roll it back. 2. Make the ledger dedup on provider event_id, using a unique constraint on transactions.event_id together with a check-and-insert in the same transaction. 3. Reverse the duplicate posting of evt_000281 (transaction 282) with a compensating entry, then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The data repair touches only the ledger entries for pay_000259. If the wrong transaction is reversed, the books stay off. Rolling back ledger-consumer would pause its consumption while it restarts, and the lag would catch up afterwards. A constraint change could make consumer inserts fail if older duplicates already exist.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Reverse the compensating entry. Redeploy the previous ledger-consumer settings. Drop the new constraint if it causes insert failures.

proposed.why: This is the last step. The evidence shows a provider redelivery that got past the ledger's dedup, and deploy data was unavailable.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The provider redelivered the webhook for evt_000281 (payment.succeeded, pay_000259, $157.18), 0.5 s apart. webhook-receiver queued both deliveries, at partition 1 offsets 120 and 121. ledger-consumer booked both, as transactions 281 and 282. That puts the ledger $157.18 ahead of the provider and fails posted_exactly_once and matches_provider. payment-confirmer saw the same duplicate and correctly returned already_confirmed, so the fault is in the ledger's idempotency: it did not dedup on provider event_id. It does report already_processed for some events, so it may dedup by Kafka offset rather than event_id, but that is unconfirmed. Deploys could not be read, because Docker did not answer, so whether a ledger-consumer change caused this is open. The money check found no other affected events.

evidence.shows: After settling, evt_000281 is posted twice (transactions 281 and 282). The ledger is 15,718 cents over the provider, all on pay_000259. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000281 twice: at 20:08:00.097 to offset 120 and at 20:08:00.604 to offset 121, with different traces.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000281 at both offsets.
For offset 121, ledger-consumer inserted the transaction and its entries and reported outcome 'posted'. payment-confirmer's outcome was already_confirmed.
In the last 10 minutes the ledger reported 17 already_processed and 485 posted, so its dedup catches some duplicates but missed this one.
ledger-consumer logged no warnings or errors in the last hour, so the duplicate posting raised nothing.
recent_deploys failed because Docker did not answer, so no deploy or handler setting could be checked.

proposed_fix.summary: 1. When Docker responds, check recent_deploys for a ledger-consumer LEDGER_HANDLER change, and roll it back if one exists. 2. Make the ledger dedup on provider event_id, with a unique constraint on transactions.event_id and the check-and-insert in one transaction. 3. Reverse duplicate transaction 282 with a compensating entry, then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The repair touches only the ledger entries for pay_000259. Reversing the wrong transaction would leave the books off. A rollback pauses ledger consumption while the container restarts. A new unique constraint could make inserts fail if older duplicates already exist.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Reverse the compensating entry. Redeploy the prior ledger-consumer settings. Drop the constraint if it causes insert failures.
